description: Curated eval set for engine QUALITY measurement. Distinct from regression_baseline.json (which measures Jaccard DRIFT on output stability) — this scores actual result quality against hand-annotated ground truth. Every query gets run through the engine on eval runs; scoring: (1) precision@3 against ideal_top_3, (2) coverage@10 against ideal ∪ acceptable, (3) violation flag if any must_not_appear title surfaces. Categories break out per-report so we can see e.g. 'known-failure mean precision improved from 0.1 → 0.4 across the fan-service subset.' First-pass curation by Claude 2026-08-26 pending review.

categories.vibe-anchor: Queries known to work well historically — regression targets. If these get worse, we broke something.
categories.known-failure: Queries from the journal that returned empty or wrong results. Fixing these is the direct engine-improvement target.
categories.franchise-title: Users typing exact show titles into FaS. COA A adds a hint; engine should ALSO return the show itself + related shows so users who ignore the hint still get value.
categories.slt-anchor: Shows-Like-This reference sets with expected thematic overlap. Tests the DNA/triangulation pipeline.
categories.hidden-gems: Queries that test whether the engine surfaces non-mainstream shows (COA C context — 4x mainstream skew is the underlying concern).
categories.intuition: User-flagged 'should work but doesn't' queries — first-class input from your months of hands-on experience, not derived from journal data. Populate during review.

id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for the query entry. Convention: <category-prefix>-<descriptive-slug>. Used for stable references in scoring output, PR discussion, and git blame. Never reuse an id even after a query is retired.

query.description: The natural-language query text as a user would type it. NULL for shows_like_this mode (see reference_titles instead).

mode.description: Which search surface the query targets. Determines which engine entry point runs during eval.

filters.description: UI-level filters applied at submit. Passed through to the engine identically to how the FaS/SLT frontend passes them. All keys present; use null / 'All' for 'no filter'.

lens.description: FaS lens selector. NULL for shows_like_this mode.

era.description: Decade filter. 'All' = no restriction. NULL for shows_like_this mode.

rating_max.description: Content rating ceiling. NULL = no restriction. Only applies to Intelligent Search lens.

reference_titles.description: 1-3 canonical anime titles for SLT mode. Omit for other modes. Titles must exactly match how the show is stored in the vault (english_title or romaji_title).

negative_anchors.description: 0-2 titles the user wants the results to AVOID resembling. Omit or empty array when unused.

category.description: Classifier for eval aggregation. Scoring reports break out per-category so we can see e.g. 'known-failure mean precision improved from 0.1 → 0.4.' See top-level categories object for definitions.

source.description: Provenance of the query. Free-form but favor structured markers: 'journal-YYYY-MM' for extraction from search_journal (append '(returned empty)' or '(worked well)' as observed), 'user-remembered' for queries you recall using, 'user-intuition' for gut-flagged should-work cases, 'anchor-test' for engineered anchors. Multiple sources joined with '+'.

ideal_top_3.description: The 3 titles a well-behaved engine SHOULD surface in top-3 for this query. Ordered by expected desirability. Titles must match vault storage exactly. Used as the numerator for precision@3 scoring. Empty array acceptable when the query is CORRECTLY empty (too vague to score) OR when confidence=low and ideal set is genuinely unknowable — flag both cases in notes.

acceptable_top_10.description: Additional titles that would be REASONABLE to see in top-10 alongside the ideals. Doesn't count against the score to include; boosts coverage@10 when present. Ordered by rough preference but ordering isn't scored.

must_not_appear.description: Negative constraints. Titles whose surfacing would signal a bug (leaked series sibling, off-vibe result, off-topic show). Empty array is normal; populate when there's a specific failure mode to guard against. Any hit is a hard fail on this query (violation flag).

confidence.description: Honesty flag about the ground-truth values (ideal_top_3 / acceptable_top_10). 'high' = curator has strong domain knowledge and stands by the set. 'medium' = educated guess, plausible but not authoritative. 'low' = pure speculation, please double-check before trusting per-query scores. Aggregate reports may weight or filter by confidence.

notes.description: Free-form context. Why this query is in the set, what specific engine behavior it tests, any live-observation baseline (e.g., 'live run 2026-08-26 returned X at top'), corrections history, or curator uncertainty flags. Not machine-consumed but load-bearing for future review sessions.

Vague one-word query 'Dark'. Pre-COA-B this entry tested 'engine correctly returns empty' — that was implicitly testing the safety-block-produces-empty path. Post-COA-B, composite fallback returns 8-15 semantically-close candidates and the low_confidence banner fires (surfaces as [low_conf] in the eval console output). Reshape: coverage-only guard against retrieval nonsense. acceptable_top_10 lists canonical dark anime a competent semantic engine should surface for a one-word 'Dark' query; must_not_appear lists obvious anti-thematic shows (moe/SoL/comedy) whose appearance would indicate popularity bias overriding thematic matching. Zero coverage is not a hard failure (the space of 'dark' anime is wide), but zero-plus-violations is. Banner-fires signal is captured in engine_meta.low_confidence per record; grade manually via console output or a follow-on eval-runner extension.

observations.note: 5-run probe post-COA-B. Distribution: n=13/14/15/13/15 (min 13, max 15, always non-empty). 1/5 runs safety-blocked → composite fallback fired cleanly with lc=True/fb='composite' in 9.1s (vs 17-20s for non-blocked runs). The pre-COA-B 08-30 empty pool + 5.34s elapsed fingerprint was a safety-blocked run before the composite fallback path existed. Plan hypothesis ('rerank-cuts-all, not safety-block') was wrong; the mechanism IS PROHIBITED_CONTENT and COA B already handles it. Also observed: none of the current ideal_top_3 (Ergo Proxy / GITS:SAC / Lain) surface in top-5 across the 5 runs; reranker consistently prefers ID:INVADED / From the New World / Death Note / Pluto / Terror in Resonance. That's a separate reranker-quality question about which sci-fi/psych canon this pair anchors to; the intermittence question is closed.

Decade-filter enforcement bug root-caused and fixed. `_detect_studio` was capturing 'TV' from 'TV series' as a studio via Pattern 2, injecting `studio LIKE '%TV%'` into the SQL WHERE clause → zero rows → silent fallback to unfiltered path → 2005-2026 shows leaked through. Fix: added TV/OVA/ONA/movie/film/special to `_NON_STUDIO_TERMS`. Post-fix probe returns 15/15 shows in 1990-1999. Secondary discovery: only Berserk from the current ideal_top_3 has MAL's 'Seinen' genre tag — NGE/Lain/Cowboy Bebop/Utena use Avant Garde/Psychological/Drama instead (MAL taxonomy quirk: Seinen is a publishing demographic, narrower than 'thematically mature'). The 'mature themes' → seinen concept synonym plus Seinen genre filter narrows the pool aggressively. Consider revising ideal/acceptable to Berserk-heavy, or reshape query to remove the 'mature themes' constraint if we want NGE/Lain/Cowboy Bebop in the pool.
